title: One hundred and fourteen
hookLine: 114 surahs, arranged mostly longest to shortest, not by date

lines: THE FIRST WORD IS NEAR THE BACK.
cards: Open a mushaf for the first time and you might expect it to start where the story starts: the cave, the angel, the first word, iqra'. It doesn't. That first word is near the very back, in Surah 96.

The book opens with al-Fatiha, seven short verses, then the longest surah of all, al-Baqarah. From there the surahs get shorter, more or less, until the tiny ones at the end that you walked through in camp four.

teach.b: The Qur'an has one hundred and fourteen surahs, or chapters. Scholars aren't certain where the word surah comes from. Some connect it to sur, a city wall, so a surah is a section fenced off.
Others link it to a row of stones in a building, or to a rank, a step up. The Qur'an itself uses the word when it challenges those who doubted it to bring a single surah like it.

teach.h: ALL BUT ONE OPEN WITH BISMILLAH
teach.b: Every surah but one opens with bismillah; the ninth, al-Tawbah, begins without it. Each has a name, usually taken from a striking word inside it: the Cow, the Bee, the Spider, the Fig.
And here's what surprises most first-time readers: the surahs aren't arranged in the order they were revealed.
After al-Fatiha, they run roughly from longest to shortest. Roughly: there are exceptions, but the pattern is plain.
So the earliest revelations, short and urgent, sit mostly at the back, and many of the long later ones at the front. Why this order?
Most scholars hold that the order of verses within each surah was set by the Prophet ﷺ himself, as Jibril taught him. On the order of the surahs, scholars differ.

Many say that too was taught by the Prophet; others say it was partly arranged by the companions, following what they knew of his recitation. Either way, Muslims read the order as meaningful, not accidental.
You can open anywhere and begin. A child can start at the short end, as you did. The book isn't a timeline.
It's more like a house of rooms, each with its own door.

how: Muslims know the surahs by name and number; children usually learn them from the short end of the book first, and a printed mushaf lists all 114 with their names.

games.q: you open a mushaf to find the very first revelation, iqra'. where do you look?
games.why: it's Surah 96, near the back. the book isn't a timeline: after the opening, the surahs run roughly longest to shortest.

practice: Open a mushaf, on paper or on your phone, and find the list of surahs, at the back of many Arabic copies, at the front of many English ones.
Let your eye run slowly down it, al-Baqarah, Al Imran, an-Nisa, al-Ma'idah, all the way to an-Nas, number one hundred and fourteen, and notice where the ones you know are sitting.
If there's no copy near you, picture the line of them, long rooms giving way to small ones.
